facts.text: "Proven in use" under ISO 26262-8:2018 clause 14 and IEC 61508 is a route to claim compliance for a reused element.
facts.quote: "Proven in use" (ISO 26262-8:2018 clause 14; IEC 61508) is a route to claim compliance for a *reused element*.

facts.text: A proven-in-use compliance claim requires the reused element's definition and conditions of use to be identical or highly similar to its field use, plus a justified service period.
facts.quote: It requires that the element's definition and conditions of use be identical, or highly similar, to its use in the field, plus a justified service period.

facts.text: The ISO 26262 proven-in-use formula is based on a 70% confidence level.
facts.quote: The ISO 26262 formula is based on a 70% confidence level

facts.text: IEC 61508 proven-in-use practice uses a higher confidence level than the 70% confidence level used in the ISO 26262 formula.
facts.quote: The ISO 26262 formula is based on a 70% confidence level; IEC 61508 practice uses higher confidence.

facts.text: Proven-in-use evidence does not validate a simulator.
facts.quote: It does not validate a simulator

facts.text: Adding automatic braking changes the item, so an existing warning system's field history does not transfer to the braking function.
facts.quote: adding automatic braking changes the item, so the warning system's history does not transfer to the braking function.
